headline: Flash flood tears down a Himalayan valley on the Nepal–China border, with hundreds unaccounted for
dek: A wall of water swept the Bhote Koshi valley in Nepal's Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning. Officials suspect the cause was not rain but an ice-and-rock avalanche across the border in Tibet — the second such flood on this river system in fourteen months.
summary: A flash flood struck Nepal's Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning, destroying hydropower plants and bridges on a major route to Tibet. Officials say several people have died and hundreds of travellers are unaccounted for; the toll is provisional and rising.

image.alt: A fast-flowing mountain river carrying sediment through a steep valley

body.text: At around nine o'clock on Wednesday morning, a flash flood came down the Bhote Koshi river valley in Nepal's Rasuwa district, on the border with Tibet. It destroyed hydropower plants, bridges, a police area office and a stretch of the main road that carries traders and tourists between Nepal and China. Several people are confirmed dead. Hundreds more — travellers, drivers, security personnel — are unaccounted for.

The market town of Syaphrubesi took the worst of it, according to the Kathmandu Post. The nearby settlement of Timure was also hit, and the surge continued downstream into the Trishuli and Narayani river systems.

What makes this flood unusual is that it does not appear to have been caused by rain falling where it landed. Sanjeev Adhikari, a meteorologist quoted by the Kathmandu Post, said the flooding "did not appear to have been caused by heavy rainfall in Rasuwa itself." Nepali authorities suspect the trigger was an ice-and-rock avalanche or the sudden collapse of a landslide-dammed lake on the Tibetan side of the border — an event that would have given people downstream almost no warning at all.
A related mudslide struck Gyirong county on the Chinese side of the border the same morning. Xinhua, the Chinese state news agency, reported "major casualties" there without giving a figure.
The numbers, and why they keep changing

By the middle of Wednesday, Nepali officials cited by Al Jazeera and NPR put the confirmed death toll at eight or more. The Kathmandu Post's earlier report said seven. Indian outlets including The Week and Deccan Herald reported nine. None of these are in conflict, exactly — they are snapshots of the same rising number taken hours apart, which is what a toll looks like while recovery teams are still working.

The figure for the missing is larger and much less settled. Nepali authorities and Indian officials, across several outlets, described roughly 384 to 400 travellers as unaccounted for, including at least 105 Indian nationals and others from the United States, the United Kingdom, Malaysia, Australia, the Netherlands and South Africa. Reports of missing security personnel ranged from nine Armed Police Force members at Timure to a combined 41 police and armed police. No Nepali authority had issued a single reconciled figure by Wednesday evening.

body.title: Update — 26 August 2026
body.text: After this article was compiled, Al Jazeera revised its report on this event to a higher death toll. We have not independently verified the revised figure and have left the sourced numbers above as they stood when each outlet published them. For the current toll, follow the Al Jazeera link in the sources below. This is exactly the situation our [corrections policy](/corrections/) describes as an update rather than an error.
Rasuwa sits directly on the main overland route to Tibet, which is why so many people were in the flood's path on an ordinary Wednesday morning.
There could be heavy casualties or loss of property. But I cannot say for sure now.
body.cite: Narendra Pariyar, Chief District Officer of Rasuwa, speaking to Al Jazeera

body.text: Rescue helicopters could not land at first because the water was still too high. The Nepal Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police were mobilised, and Nepali Army sources told reporters that more than fifty people had been pulled out by Wednesday evening. Medical teams, Scouts and the Red Cross were coordinated into the response, and the government ordered free medical treatment for those injured.

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority convened an emergency meeting. The government formally asked both India and China for rescue assistance. Nepal's Consul General in Lhasa said Chinese authorities had been unable to re-establish contact with some border security personnel on the Tibetan side.

This is the second flood on this river system in fourteen months. Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk reduction specialist quoted by NPR, described the pattern bluntly: "The Lhende Khola has flooded twice in fourteen months, this time triggered by an ice rock avalanche."

The geography is the problem. The Bhote Koshi rises in Tibet, becomes the Trishuli in Nepal and eventually the Gandak in India. An event high in the mountains on one side of an international border arrives as a wall of water on the other, and the warning systems do not cross the frontier as fast as the water does. A comparable Nepali flood in 2025 was traced to the draining of a lake perched on a glacier in Tibet.
Rasuwa district is home to roughly 50,000 people. Nepal is also in the middle of a monsoon season that has already been lethal across South Asia.

body.title: A note on names
body.text: Following our editorial standards, this article does not name any private individual killed, missing or rescued. The people named here are public officials and specialists speaking in their professional capacity.

uncertain: The death toll. Same-day reports ranged from seven to nine and the figure was still rising; no single reconciled official number had been issued.
How many people are missing. Counts of travellers ranged from roughly 384 to 400, and counts of missing security personnel from nine to 41, across different authorities.
The cause. A glacial lake outburst, an ice-and-rock avalanche and a landslide dam-burst were all under consideration; no geological authority had confirmed which.
The full picture on the Chinese side of the border, where Xinhua reported 'major casualties' without a figure.
